title: Verbal Adverbs 7: Negating Gerunds with не
description: Negate a verbal adverb by placing не directly before it as a separate word (не зная, не понимая, не глядя), avoiding the незная fusion error, and choose the aspect of the negated gerund by timing.
descriptionRussian: Отрицание деепричастия: частица «не» ставится прямо перед ним отдельным словом (не зная, не понимая, не глядя); нельзя писать слитно (незная); вид негативного деепричастия выбирается по времени действия.
intro: Negating one of these is simple and carries two traps. The negative word stays separate, unlike participles and adjectives where it fuses on. And the preposition meaning 'without' is not a substitute: it takes a noun, not a verb form. Three negated verbal adverbs are near-fixed phrases you will meet constantly.
rules: Negate a gerund by placing не directly before it as a SEPARATE word: не зная, не понимая, не глядя.
Never fuse не into the gerund: незная is wrong. Unlike participles and adjectives (незнающий), a gerund keeps не separate, like не знал, не смотрит.
Не зная, не понимая, and не глядя are everyday near-fixed B2 phrases.
Choose aspect by timing: a negated imperfective gerund is a state of not-doing during the main action (не понимая); a negated perfective is something not completed before it (rarer).
Do not swap in без: без takes a genitive noun (без знания), not a gerund. To negate the action, use не + gerund.
examples: Не зная ответа, она молчала. (Not knowing the answer, she stayed silent.)
Не понимая инструкций, Иван попросил помощи. (Not understanding the instructions, Ivan asked for help.)
Не глядя на часы, Антон работал до утра. (Without looking at the clock, Anton worked until morning.)
Не дождавшись ответа, она ушла. (Not having waited for an answer, she left - negated perfective.)
Без знания языка трудно жить за границей. (Without knowledge of the language it is hard to live abroad - без + genitive noun, NOT a gerund.)

items.prompt: How is negation marked on a verbal adverb?
items.promptEnglish: Where does the не particle go?
options: Directly before the gerund, separately: не зная
Negation is impossible; rewrite with когда
items.answer: Directly before the gerund, separately: не зная
items.hint: Negation works the same way as on any verb form.
items.explanation: The particle не sits directly before the gerund, as a separate word, just as with finite verbs and infinitives: не зная, не понимая, не глядя. The other options describe non-existent patterns; gerund negation is fully regular.

items.prompt: Why is незная wrong but незнающий acceptable?
items.promptEnglish: Why can a participle fuse не but a gerund cannot?
options: A gerund is a verb form and keeps не separate; a participle behaves like an adjective and can fuse
items.answer: A gerund is a verb form and keeps не separate; a participle behaves like an adjective and can fuse
items.hint: Think about whether each word patterns like a verb or like an adjective.
items.explanation: A gerund is a verb form, so не stays separate, exactly as in не знал, не смотрит: не зная. A participle behaves like an adjective and can fuse не into one word (незнающий студент). The gerund never fuses; незная is an error.

items.promptEnglish: Not knowing the answer, Masha stayed silent.
items.hint: Negation goes directly before the gerund, as a separate word.
items.explanation: Не зная is the standard negated imperfective gerund of знать, with не a separate word. Незная fuses the particle, which Russian does not do with a verb form; 'Знав не' has the wrong word order; без takes a genitive noun (без знания), not a gerund.

items.promptEnglish: Not understanding the instructions, Anton asked for help.
items.hint: The slot needs a negated imperfective gerund (the not-understanding holds during the asking).
items.explanation: Не понимая is the negated imperfective gerund of понимать. The not-understanding is a state simultaneous with the asking. Не понимать is the negated infinitive; не понимал is the negated finite past; не понять is the negated perfective infinitive.

items.prompt: _____ ответа, она ушла. (She didn't wait for an answer and left.)
items.promptEnglish: Not having waited for an answer, she left.
items.hint: A completed non-action before the main verb: negated PERFECTIVE gerund (-вшись).
items.explanation: Не дождавшись is the negated perfective gerund: the not-waiting is completed before она ушла (she left without having waited). Не дожидаясь (imperfective) would stress the ongoing not-waiting; не дождаться is the infinitive; не дождалась is a finite past verb.

blanks: _____ на часы, Антон работал до утра. (Without looking at the clock, Anton worked until morning.)
_____ языка, трудно жить за границей. (Without knowledge of the language, it is hard to live abroad.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: (1) Не глядя is a near-fixed negated imperfective gerund ('without looking'), with не separate. (2) 'Without knowledge' as a thing is без + genitive noun: без знания (not a gerund).
hints: The not-looking holds during the working: negated imperfective gerund, не separate.
Here 'without X' is a noun, so use без + genitive.

errorCorrection.sentence: Невидя дороги в темноте, мы шли медленно.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Not seeing the road in the dark, we walked slowly.
errorCorrection.explanation: Russian negates a gerund by placing не directly before it as a separate word: не видя. Невидя fuses the particle, which Russian orthography does not allow for a verb form (unlike adjectives, where невидимый is fine). Без видя is impossible: без takes nouns.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Not listening to the advice, Anton did it his own way.
errorCorrection.explanation: Negation on a gerund is the separate particle не before the form: не слушая. Неслушая fuses не into the gerund, which Russian does not do with a verb form. Не слушать is a negated infinitive, which cannot serve as the backgrounded-action clause.

errorCorrection.sentence: Без помня адреса, мы долго искали дом.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Not remembering the address, we searched for the house a long time.
errorCorrection.explanation: To negate the ACTION with a gerund, use не + gerund: не помня адреса. Без cannot take a gerund: без помня and без помнить are both impossible. If you wanted the noun construction, it would be без адреса ('without the address').

errorCorrection.sentence: Не спрашивая разрешения, он взял ключи и ушёл навсегда.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Without having asked permission, he took the keys and left for good.
errorCorrection.explanation: The taking and leaving form a single completed sequence after a permission that was never obtained, so the negated PERFECTIVE gerund fits: не спросив разрешения. Не спрашивая is the imperfective ('while not asking'), which frames a background instead of a completed non-event.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Not knowing the answer, she stayed silent.
minimalPairs.explanation: Russian negates the gerund with the particle не placed directly before it: не зная. Без takes a genitive noun and would need a different construction (без знания), not a gerund.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Without knowledge of the language, it is hard to work here.
minimalPairs.explanation: Без governs a NOUN in the genitive, never a gerund: без знания языка. Зная is the gerund, and it can only be negated with не (не зная языка), never introduced by без.

sentenceBuilding.answer: Не зная адреса, Антон позвонил другу
sentenceBuilding.translation: Not knowing the address, Anton called his friend.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Keep не a separate word right before the imperfective gerund зная.

sentenceBuilding.answer: Не глядя по сторонам, она перешла дорогу
sentenceBuilding.translation: Without looking around, she crossed the road.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Не глядя is a near-fixed negated imperfective gerund; не stays separate.

sentenceBuilding.translation: Not understanding the question, Lena stayed quiet.
sentenceBuilding.hint: The not-understanding holds during the silence: negated imperfective gerund.

sentenceBuilding.answer: Не дождавшись автобуса, мы пошли пешком
sentenceBuilding.translation: Not having waited for the bus, we walked.
sentenceBuilding.hint: A completed non-action before the main verb: negated perfective gerund не дождавшись.

patternRecognition.question: Why is не written separately from зная?
options: A gerund is a verb form, so не stays a separate word
It is a typo; it should be незная
patternRecognition.answer: A gerund is a verb form, so не stays a separate word
patternRecognition.explanation: A gerund is a verb form, and verb forms keep не separate (не знал, не смотрит, не зная). Only adjective-like words such as participles can fuse не (незнающий). So не зная, never незная.

patternRecognition.sentence: Без знания языка трудно жить за границей.
patternRecognition.question: Why is this без + знания, not не зная?
options: без takes a genitive noun (знания), not a gerund
не зная would also be spelled без зная
patternRecognition.answer: без takes a genitive noun (знания), not a gerund
patternRecognition.explanation: Без governs a noun in the genitive: без знания языка. It can never take a gerund (без зная is impossible). To negate the action you would use the gerund не зная; to express 'without X' as a thing, use без + a genitive noun.

patternRecognition.question: Why is the gerund perfective (дождавшись) here?
options: The not-waiting is completed before she left
The main verb is present tense
patternRecognition.answer: The not-waiting is completed before she left
patternRecognition.explanation: The negated perfective gerund Не дождавшись marks a completed non-event before the main verb: she did not wait, then left. A negated imperfective (не дожидаясь) would frame the not-waiting as ongoing instead.

reviewVocab.definition: negate a gerund by placing не directly before it as a separate word: не зная, не понимая, не глядя. A gerund is a verb form, so не never fuses (незная is wrong).
reviewVocab.example: Не зная ответа, она молчала. Не глядя на часы, он работал.

reviewVocab.definition: a gerund keeps не separate (verb form: не зная), while a participle/adjective can fuse it (незнающий студент). Do not write незная.
без takes a genitive noun (без знания, без помощи), a different construction from the negated gerund. To negate the action, use не + gerund.
reviewVocab.example: Без знания языка трудно; но: не зная языка, он растерялся.
